quotes.race: Prix Royal-Oak (Group 1) (3yo+) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: It's always something to win a Group 1 at any stage of the year. What Double Major has done there is just mad. He had the perfect trip, having his own way up front and by the time they got to the false straight, he already had the others on the stretch, while Maxime hadn't yet moved. I wondered what he'd find but he accelerated regardless of the ground and he's just a crack, a very, very good horse. We'll have to think about what we want to do. He's entitled to a holiday now and he'll need some downtime after that effort and the others during the season. We'll make a decision about where we want to go, whether we want to have a crack at Dubai or not - Christophe Ferland, trainer.

runners.breeder: S C E A Du Haras Des Sablonnets Et Al
runners.comment: Battled on well for narrow win at Musselburgh last month; this track also suits him
runners.spotlight: 12 chase wins, the latest when battling on well to lead close home at Musselburgh (2m7f, good to soft) three weeks ago; not very reliable nowadays but is only 2lb higher here and this track also suits him.

quotes.race: Secret Garden And Gd's Pooley Bridge Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Red Happy has done well for us all right. We got him from David Pipe the week after he won his last race for him, and we couldn't be happier that he's stayed in good form. It helps a lot when you get a horse who can keep going like he does. He toughed that out and didn't miss a single jump ? he jumped for fun when they were out in the country. We'll keep him on the go and see what the handicapper does - George Bewley, trainer.

runners.comment: Placed off 3lb higher on latest outing in January 2024; player if fully tuned up
runners.spotlight: 3-7 since blinkers were added in February 2023; creditable third in North Yorkshire Grand National at Catterick (3m6f, soft) on latest outing in January 2024 and resumes on 3lb lower mark; player if fully tuned up.

quotes.race: Living North Magazines Handicap Chase (Go North Red Rum Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I had a walk on the track earlier and I just felt like right down the inside was maybe where it was wettest so I tried to keep out in the middle. Court At Slip does whatever you want him to - if you want him come big for you he will do but if you leave him alone he's clever - William Easterby, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Won from the front over 2m4f here last month and is unexposed over 3m under rules
runners.spotlight: Returned to form with front-running success here (2m4f, good to soft) last month and is now 4-17 over fences; recent 5lb rise demands a bit more from him but he's completely unexposed over 3m under rules.

quotes.race: Watch Racing TV Now Handicap Chase (Go North Monet's Garden Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I just had to try and get Hello Judge in a rhythm and it was good to see him get back to form. The stable has been a bit quiet lately but hopefully that's them turning the corner - Danny McMenamin, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Has been in the doldrums but combination of ease in grade and new tongue-tie offers hope
runners.spotlight: Out of form last season and has also disappointed on both outings this term but drops in grade today and might be aided by new tongue-tie (reportedly made respiratory noise last time); dangerous to ignore.

stable_tour.quote: We're not sure whether she'll quite come back. She got stuck in the mud when pulled up in the Borders National at Kelso last time. She's had her wind done, but that kind of ground can test any wind. She's very small and needs things to fall into place. She's right down the handicap and it would be nice to try to find another race for her to win, then see where we are. The Edinburgh National is probably too sharp for her and she won't be easy to place over the next few months. 22-01-25

runners.owner: Dennis J Coppola & Mrs Dianne Sayer
runners.comment: Good second over hurdles in January but well held since; now 0-10 under rules
runners.spotlight: 0-10 under rules; ran game race in defeat over hurdles at Wetherby (3m, soft) in January but ought to have coped better with the heavy ground when well beaten at Ayr (2m4f) last month and he's 3lb out of the weights for this return to chasing.

runners.comment: Ran okay over C&D in first-time visor last month; 5lb wrong today; blinkers now tried
runners.spotlight: Runs this track well but has been well below his best this season; seemingly perked up by change of headgear when respectable sixth over C&D (soft) in first-time visor last month but is effectively 2lb higher from out of the weights today; blinkers given a whirl this time.

quotes.race: Go North Monet's Garden Series Final Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Uptown Harry ran terribly at Newcastle but the ground was jarring and he didn't let himself down on it, but he ran a solid race back here next time and we knew we were on the right track. We prayed for rain for a month and we managed to get it. We were pretty confident today. We knew he'd love the ground and he loves going right handed. And this is his track - they just don't put enough races on for him! - Jane Walton, trainer.

racecards.race_name: Blackwell Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qualifier)

runners.comment: Has not kicked on from her winning hurdle debut in October; beaten 25l in first handicap
runners.spotlight: Won Exeter maiden (2m, good) on hurdling debut in October but has not kicked on since; beaten about 25l (albeit in better race than this) when fifth of seven on last month's handicap debut at Kempton (2m, good to soft) and clearly needs to do better here.

quotes.race: Rhino.Bet Proudly Sponsor Henry Brooke Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Roaring Home is a nice filly. Henry (Daly, trainer) did say to me she'll just lack a bit of fitness and she had a good blow turning in, so I switched her in to try and save a bit and have one go at the horse in front. I was surprised how well she picked up and she's got an awful lot of improvement to come - Harry Cobden, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Veteran who scored over C&D last month and now bids to complete a hat-trick
runners.spotlight: Veteran who is probably best known as a Market Rasen specialist but looked as good as ever when scoring by over 7l over C&D (good to soft) three weeks ago; now bids to complete a hat-trick; respected in current form.

prev_owners.owner: Ecurie HDBB, N Clement & Mrs Linda Dyer

runners.comment: Largely consistent mare; form of last month's Bangor sixth can be upgraded; shortlisted
runners.spotlight: Largely consistent since her Ludlow novice win (2m, good) last May and ran better than finishing position suggests when sixth at Bangor (2m, soft; first-time cheekpieces) last month, where she made a bad jumping error four flights out; might be the answer.

runners.comment: Not beaten far on hurdling debut but both runs since were very disappointing; h'cap debut
runners.spotlight: Not beaten far when fourth of seven behind useful winner on hurdle debut at Ayr (2m, good to soft) in October but both runs this year (2m4f/2m3f, soft) have been very disappointing; drops back in trip for handicap debut; may still have potential but others have much less to prove.

stable_tour.quote: A really nice mare from the family of Oscar Whisky and Seeyouatmidnight. She ran well in bumpers and was slightly disappointing at Ayr last time, but we're not sure if she stayed the trip. If it was soft ground, I could see her going to the Herring Queen Final at Kelso. We'll have to try to get her qualified, but it's big money and she could go well there. 22-01-25

runners.owner: Mrs I C Sellars And Miss D C Sellars

prev_owners.owner: Mrs I C Sellars & Major Philip Arkwright

runners.comment: Chased home much improved rival at Newcastle in December; remains on good mark
runners.spotlight: Out of form in early part of this season but returned from break with good effort at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft), travelling well before succumbing to a much-improved rival; remains on a good mark; major player.

runners.breeder: Mrs D W Davenport & Mr D Obank
runners.comment: Yet to build upon mildly encouraging hurdle debut but remains unexposed
runners.spotlight: Yet to build upon mildly encouraging hurdle debut in November but remains unexposed and has a lowly mark for this handicap debut; could have a say.

runners.comment: Second stable run was much better than her debut but she still makes only limited appeal
runners.spotlight: High-mileage 9yo who had modest hurdling strike-rate when trained in Ireland and was well beaten on last month's stable debut; fared better when keeping-on fourth behind Lady Babs over C&D a few days later but still makes only limited appeal.

prev_owners.owner: Exors of the Late Nicholas Kelly

runners.comment: 0-22 over hurdles but twice cam second last month; headgear switched today
runners.spotlight: 0-22 over hurdles but came second on consecutive outings last month, latterly at Musselburgh (1m7f, good to soft); will play another significant role if change of headgear has any positive effect here (usually visored).

runners.comment: Lowly rated Flat maiden who has not shown much over hurdles; 7lb wrong for handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Lowly rated Flat maiden who has not shown a great deal on her three hurdling starts this season; 7lb out of the weights for this handicap debut; significant improvement required.

stable_tour.quote: She's quite a nice three-year-old filly and I think she'll improve. She's been a wee bit unfortunate. She was supposed to run in a race at Musselburgh that was cancelled, so she's entered at Hamilton this week to give her a spin round there. She was second on her first run for us at Newcastle in March but was then seventh, beaten just over eight lengths, in a tough race that didn't really work for us. I think she'll want a trip - she'll maybe go 1m4f with a view that she might go juvenile hurdling. 16-05-24

racecards.race_name: Cocklakes Open Hunters' Chase

runners.comment: Wellbeing is an issue and has to concede weight all round on this return to hunter chasing
runners.spotlight: His sixth win under rules when taking a 2m5f handicap chase at Hereford last May for Neil Mulholland; pulled up over hurdles on his final run for that yard and has to concede weight all round on this return to hunter chasing.

stable_tour.quote: He's back in. We might look at the Aintree Foxhunters' with him if we can get him qualified in time. It's not guaranteed but a possibility. He ran well around Market Rasen and his form is good. He should make his presence felt in races like the Summer Plate. 06-03-24

runners.comment: Won his last two points but he's relying on the best of these being below par
runners.spotlight: Makes a belated return to rules action on the back of two point wins but he's relying on the best of these being below par.

quotes.race: Club Albion Juvenile Hurdle
quotes.quote: Diable De Sivola had shown ability at home and jumped really well so we were hopeful of a big run on his debut. He has won well - Lizzie Kelly, jockey.

runners.comment: Ran well to a point on hunter chase debut and may have needed it after a year out
runners.spotlight: Useful in his prime; ran well to a point on his hunter chase debut (3m, soft) and could have needed the run after a year out; should go well.

quotes.race: Guildford Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Minella Trump is best suited by good ground and afterwards I suggested he could return for a spring campaign. He's answered every question and hopefully there's more improvement - Brian Hughes, jockey.

quotes.race: MansionBet Faller Insurance Novices' Hurdle
quotes.quote: Minella Trump is a grand sort of horse. He was a bit green but he's done it nicely and he'll stay further - Brian Hughes, jockey

stable_tour.quote: A wonderful horse who won nine out of ten races at one point. We might go hunter chasing with him, and you could imagine him running a really big race in the Foxhunters' at Aintree. 12-11-24

They don't come any more genuine and consistent than this lovely horse (left) who has won nine of his last ten races, which is quite some record. During that period his rating has risen from 123 to 149, but judging by his last run he has not stopped improving yet. He had a well-earned break after his last win at Perth but he is back in fast wor k again now and the plan is to have one run and then go for the Grand National. The thing with him is that he knows how to win, he stays 3m well and you would never get a more tough and honest horse than him. I would dearly love to run him in the great race for my biggest supporter Tim Leslie. He has definitely earned a crack at the Grand National and how good he is I would not know. Obviously I have won the Grand National before and been associated with several winners of the great race, but it has changed so much over the years that there are different requirements to win it now. I think he is well worth his place, and while he is still progressing he will hopefully give us plenty to look forward to. 09-02-23

runners.comment: Had only two races since winning two points in 2022 and has a lot to find on these terms
runners.spotlight: Had only two races since winning two points in 2022 and has a lot to find on these terms.

runners.comment: Class act back in the day and did win his penultimate start in points
runners.spotlight: Class act back in the day and took care of the odds-on favourite in his penultimate point; was a remote second when refusing late on in his last, though the winner was the still-useful Allmankind; dropping back to 2m4f should be favourable.

quotes.race: bet365 Oaksey Chase (Grade 2) (For The Menorah Challenge Trophy) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was a nice win. He was entitled to win a race like that. I think he stays but I don't think we've had him quite right. We're learning all the time and I think we can get him fitter next year. I'm convinced he wants three and he galloped all the way to the line. We weren't trying to pinch an easy lead but Harry said he was going to try to make the running after Aintree. He loves good ground. He'll definitely go back to the KG but knowing him a bit more hopefully he can go somewhere else [perhaps the Charlie Hall]. I'm convinced the trip will be no problem. He galloped all the way to the line today. We changed the routine after Ascot and there are things we can do to eke a bit more improvement out of him. Paul Nicholls, trainer

quotes.race: Randox Health Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: This was a big drop in class for Saint Calvados but after having a wind operation on his summer break we wanted to give him an easier start. We knew he loves these conditions and he has handled the track. I have no idea where he will go next - Harry Whittington, trainer

quotes.race: Betfair Tingle Creek Chase (Grade 1)
quotes.quote: Saint Calvados has probably run a career best to finish third. Gavin said that when Un De Sceaux quickened we were flat out. We'll look to move up to two and a half miles now - Harry Whittington, trainer.

quotes.race: Poplar Square Chase (Grade 3)
quotes.quote: Saint Calvados is only five and super exciting. He was just a raw horse last season, he's a much stronger horse now and his work had improved significantly at home. He's much more the finished article and he'll be even stronger next year. To do it like that in that sort of company was super, and he's a proper two-miler now - Harry Whittington, trainer

quotes.race: Betway Kingmaker Novices' Chase (Grade 2)
quotes.quote: He is only five and is still improving and jumped brilliantly. Better ground will be no problem - Aidan Coleman, jockey.

quotes.race: Betfred Mobile Novices' Limited Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Saint Calvados was good and he's really exciting. Aidan felt he was sharper for the run and his jumping was tidier. Keeping him in a handicap tells us whether we're good enough for Graded races and I think we're pretty set for the Kingmaker. He's got loads of gears and I can't see any reason why we'd step him up in trip, so I think we'll take in the Kingmaker and give him an Arkle entry and go from there - Harry Whittington, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred "Racing's Biggest Supporter" Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (for The Hallowe'en Trophy)
quotes.quote: Saint Calvados is always in second gear at home and has been a natural when we schooled him at home. He is talented so hopefully we can have some fun with him. He cruised on that ground, but I don't know enough to say if he needs it. He's always going to be good on it though. He's a very big horse, strong, and Aidan mentioned the Scilly Isles, but we'll let the dust settle - Harry Whittington, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I'd had it in mind to enter him for the Charlie Hall but he's taken forever to get fit. He's still two or three weeks off a run. He's had his physical problems over the years and burst a blood vessel at Ascot last season, which may account for why he's had a reputation in the past for being a weak finisher. Once I was aware of that I started to train him differently and he regained his form in the spring, finishing fifth in the Melling Chase and then making all to win the Grade 2 Oaksey Chase on the final day of the season. That race may end up being his Gold Cup this term. This side of Christmas, I don't think we'll go for the King George again but the Peterborough Chase is a race that would suit. It's taken me the best part of a year to work this horse out but we're getting there now. 31-10-22

runners.comment: Low-grade handicapper over fences and was pulled up in a hunter chase last month
runners.spotlight: Bumper/hurdle winner but a low-grade handicapper over fences and was pulled up in a hunter chase last month.

stable_tour.quote: He won for us at Sedgefield around this time last year and was then a little bit unfortunate on a couple of occasions. He'll be competitive off his mark and the plan is to mix between hurdles and fences over the summer. 24-01-24

racecards.race_name: Kathleen Blake Memorial Mares' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Struggled in Listed grade last time; consistent (21321) in handicaps otherwise this term
runners.spotlight: Struggled in Listed grade last time; consistent record (21321) in handicaps otherwise this season, both wins at Uttoxeter (2m, good/good to soft); solid contender back down in class.

runners.breeder: S C E A De La Chaussee
runners.comment: Possibilities provided she returns to best Irish form; third run for new stable
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish mare who is a point/bumper/hurdles winner; still seeking first chase success but has possibilities off current mark provided she returns to best form; third run for new stable.

quotes.race: Congratulating Mares Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Happy D'Ex has been a bit disappointing and is one we were considering moving on. Jack said that the fast gallop suited her well. It was a nice performance. Maybe she can build on that and she will definitely jump a fence - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She was just touched off on her first start over fences at Fairyhouse. You'd have to be happy with that as a starting point, especially as she needs further than two miles. 18-10-22

runners.breeder: S A R L Haras Du Berlais & Ballantines
runners.comment: Leading contender on peak form, namely easy wins at Ludlow and Taunton in December
runners.spotlight: Placed at Ludlow last time in a stronger field than this one; leading contender on her peak form, namely easy wins at Ludlow (2m, good to soft) and Taunton (2m2f, good) in December.

racecards.race_name: Barbers Flooring Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Should be happier back at 2m after failing to stay 2m4f last time; shortlisted
runners.spotlight: Last two wins came over fences, but he has been hurdling since returning in September; should be happier back at this trip after failing to stay at Ffos Las (2m4f, heavy) last month; shortlisted down again in grade.

stable_tour.quote: He won two handicap chases last season and is at the top end of the handicap but he'll win again off a realistic mark. 24-10-24

runners.comment: 1-4 over hurdles last winter; market useful on stable debut after seven months off
runners.spotlight: 1-4 over hurdles for Alan King last winter, the win coming at Doncaster (2m1f, good to soft); changed hands for 6,500gns in November and the market should be revealing on stable debut after seven months off.

quotes.race: bet365 Juvenile Maiden Hurdle (Go North Grey Bomber Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Whispering Royal got an easy lead and put his experience from Wincanton to good use. I'm not sure how much depth there was to the race, we'll find out in a few weeks' time, but he didn't do anything wrong - Tom Cannon, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's been running with promise on the Flat and I was keen to get him started over hurdles earlier this month at Chepstow until all the rain came. Soft ground will be fine but I didn't want to start him on heavy. He's a straightforward horse and we should have a lot of fun with him. He may make his hurdling debut at Wincanton on Sunday. 25-10-23
I hope we'll have some fun with him over hurdles as he's shown promise on the Flat, and he started by finishing third at Wincanton last month. That experience will bring him on plenty. 10-11-23

runners.comment: Two wins last year; respected back in trip/grade if ready to go after 79 days off
runners.spotlight: Consistent over hurdles last year including wins at Stratford (2m, good) in July and Hereford (2m4f, good to soft) in November; didn't stay in a 0-130 contest at Ascot (2m6f, good to soft) in December, but respected back in trip/grade if ready to go after 79 days off.

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie Michel Sardou
runners.comment: Not shown much in four starts over hurdles since October; opposable despite drop in grade
runners.spotlight: Six wins on the Flat and four over hurdles, but not shown much in four starts back over jumps since October; opposable despite the drop in grade.

quotes.race: cavani.co.uk Challenger Two Mile Hurdle Series Final Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: All credit for this goes to Josh (Moore), he was adamant we should come up here with Aggagio today. He gave me my instructions, to pop him out and be very positive on him, and it's worked - Caoilin Quinn, rider.

quotes.race: Royal Sussex Regiment Handicap
quotes.quote: I don't know if there's another race back here for Aggagio. If there was he might come back, but the ground would have to be soft enough. Otherwise, he'll go jumping because his handicap mark is what it is now. He wouldn't want it bottomless over jumps - Gary Moore, trainer.

quotes.race: Sussex Roof Garden Bar Handicap
quotes.quote: Aggagio is a lovely horse. We didn't know he'd get the trip, but he's done really well. I was a bit worried about the ground if it was soft, which Goshen wants and we don't really. Gary Moore will place him where he wants and Aidan said he might get slightly further - Gary Robinson, owner.

stable_tour.quote: He did a bit of damage when he fell over fences at Plumpton in April. He's had a couple of runs back, including a spin on the Flat, and shaped okay at Wincanton over hurdles a couple of weeks ago. We'll stick over hurdles and, providing we can get his confidence back, he should do okay on slow ground. 29-10-24

runners.comment: First and third in two handicaps; unexposed and considered if coping with drying ground
runners.spotlight: Made a successful handicap debut at Leicester (2m, heavy) in January and a fair third of 11 off this mark at Bangor (2m1f, soft) last month; still unexposed and one to consider if coping with drying ground.

runners.comment: Did it well when making a successful handicap debut at Musselburgh last month; respected
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the fourth attempt over hurdles under Toby Wynne on handicap debut at Musselburgh (2m, good to soft) three weeks ago; up 8lb, but he took that race with plenty in hand and remains open to further improvement; stable won this last year.

runners.comment: Fourth in both starts over hurdles; makes handicap debut after wind surgery
runners.spotlight: Fourth of nine in both starts over hurdles since debuting for this yard in January; more needed on handicap debut, though he has undergone wind surgery since last seen.

racecards.race_name: JCB Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Useful on Flat; record of 212 over hurdles; one of the main form contenders
runners.spotlight: Below par back on Flat last time (useful in that sphere on his day); has a record of 212 over hurdles, running well at Huntingdon (2m) the final occasion; one of the main form contenders.

quotes.race: Duke Of Edinburgh Stakes (Handicap)
quotes.quote: A huge run! What can I say, I am delighted. I thought at the furlong pole that Joseph's horse had got HMS President, and just for a second, that we might come back. Bar winning, I couldn't be happier with him - Alan King, trainer.

quotes.race: Howden Handicap (Heritage Handicap)
quotes.quote: HMS President probably suits a bigger field as they do go a gallop and they come back to them if they go hard in front like they did today. He's a very talented horse and he's settled into the routine at Barbury Castle well, so we're very pleased to have him. To be honest the plan has been for quite some time to come for this today. We'll re-evaluate now and see - Robin Smith, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He had a holiday after the Ebor and, having done some decent schooling when we first got him in the spring, he's one to look forward to over hurdles. He wouldn't want deep winter ground but he's rated 101 on the Flat and is an exciting prospect for novices. 25-10-23

He's in good form and could start back over hurdles at Kempton next Monday. They took the last two flights out on his debut at Plumpton last February and that didn't suit him because he's always loved jumping and it was a long way home from the third-last - he lost a bit of interest and got outstayed. 07-11-24

runners.comment: Beaten favourite last time but had wind surgery since and may do better still
runners.spotlight: Had plenty in hand at Leicester (1m7f) on reappearance, adding to his bumper win; didn't live up to market expectations last time but had wind surgery since and may do better still.

quotes.race: 1st Airborne Division Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was ideal. Indeevar Bleu is a beautiful one to look forward to if I can keep him trainable. Hopefully he's okay in the morning and it's just a case of slowly, slowly with him. We'll go small again now in three/four weeks time, he's very raw still  but he's got a lot of ability. Olly Murphy, trainer talking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Thank You All Groundstaff For ~Groundsweek2023 Open NH Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I've always loved Indeevar Bleu but I haven't trained him for a bumper. He's taken so much time to come to himself but that was all pure raw ability today. He'll go novice hurdling next season and you won't see him until then as we want to look after him - Ollly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He had only one run last season before picking up an injury. He'll be back in a maiden hurdle and I hope he can progress into a smart novice. 24-10-24

I really love this horse and he'll start off over hurdles at Bangor or Wetherby in the next ten days. He won a bumper last season and has been jumping well at home. He'll probably want two and a half miles in time, but we'll start off at two and hopefully see him progress. 01-11-23

runners.comment: Has form figures of 3121 (bumpers/hurdles) and is open to further progress
runners.spotlight: Travelled strongly on his way to winning easily at Leicester (2m4f) and should cope with this drop back in trip; has form figures of 3121 (bumpers/hurdles) and is open to further progress.

stable_tour.quote: He bolted up in a bumper at Market Rasen in April and made a pleasing debut at Carlisle. He'll learn on the job and will definitely win his maiden and novice. 24-10-24

runners.owner: Cherry Knoll Farm, M&t Ward & D Skelton
runners.comment: Bumper form includes a solid effort; bred to do well over hurdles
runners.spotlight: Both starts in bumpers, better effort when solid second (behind useful sort) at Chepstow on debut; bred to do well over hurdles and remains open to improvement; interesting.

stable_tour.quote: He was second at Chepstow on his debut, staying on really strongly, which took us a little by surprise because his work hadn't been exceptional. He should win a bumper and go on to be a nice novice hurdler next year. 12-11-24

runners.comment: Hurdles debutant who has unconvincing claims on Flat form
runners.spotlight: Hurdles debutant who has unconvincing claims, being a regressive maiden on the Flat.

runners.comment: Dual point winner in Ireland but this looks a stiff task on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Modest completion record in Irish points but managed to win twice in November; midfield in bumper on sole rules attempt; likely has a stiff task in this field on debut for new yard.

runners.breeder: Mme Sarah Faulks & Mr Nigel Faulks
runners.comment: Disappointing on reappearance but retains potential judged on bumper form
runners.spotlight: Disappointing favourite in Ffos Las maiden hurdle (2m) on reappearance but can't be written off yet; retains potential, having been 2-3 in bumpers (won at Exeter and Huntingdon) last term.

quotes.race: PHP Architects Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was an impressive show form Dunskay who had a dirty trachea wash after his last run. That was a good performance under a penalty and he'll go for the Aintree Bumper after that - Ben Pauling, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He came back in with a wind issue so we've had to rectify that and he won't be seen until Christmas time. The only time he got beat in bumpers was when he had a dirty trach wash after the race and I think he's a big talent. He's an exceptional jumper and a chaser for the future, but he's also effective over hurdles and I'm looking forward to getting him on the track. 21-11-24

runners.owner: The Nigel Jones & Roy Ovel Syndicate
runners.comment: Hurdles debutant who needs improvement on his bumper form
runners.spotlight: Hurdles debutant who needs improvement on his bumper efforts and may be more interesting at a later stage; stable has a stronger chance with A Pai De Nom on the figures.

runners.comment: Every chance when unseating rider two out in latest Irish point start
runners.spotlight: Raced twice in Irish points, every chance when unseating rider two out latest; joined new connections for £35,000; market may offer further guidance.

runners.comment: Soundly beaten in maiden hurdle at Taunton
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten in 2m maiden hurdle at Taunton; likely one for handicaps later on.

runners.comment: Pair of duck eggs next to his name
runners.spotlight: Pair of duck eggs next to his name and is best watched.

runners.comment: Plenty to find on the figures
runners.spotlight: Plenty to find on bare figures and is likely to find better opportunities in handicaps shortly.

runners.comment: Hurdles debutant who has something to find on bumper form

runners.spotlight: Irish point winner who needs to improve sharply on his bumper effort; took a good hold in that rules run and now wears hood.

runners.spotlight: Dual Flat winner and an improving juvenile hurdler; bagged Listed honours at Musselburgh (1m7f) on penultimate start, then ran well in Grade 2 event at Kempton (2m) later in February; leading claims.

quotes.race: bet365 Scottish Triumph Hurdle (A Juvenile Hurdle) (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: St Pancras only ran a couple of weeks ago and we were anxious to get some more experience into him as quickly as possible as he's a lovely horse but just a bit novicey. We were wary even though it is a Listed race that I'd be waiting around until the end of February for some nice ground, so I'm glad we put him on the box with tomorrow's two runners. He did a lovely bit of work the other day and we're over the moon as that is our first Listed winner. We didn't think he'd have the pace of some of them as he probably wants further, but Kevin was patient and came with one good run - Toby Lawes, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a good-looking horse. He's getting there now and is nearly ready to run. 29-04-24

I always thought he was a lovely horse. He came out really well from the Ascot race, where he was fifth, and the aim was to get him plenty of experience for the spring. I couldn't see that many options for him in February that were going to be run on decent ground and, luckily, I managed to persuade Andrew Wates to let me take him up to Musselburgh for the Scottish Triumph Hurdle. He's a big, scopey horse who stayed very well on the Flat and I wasn't sure he'd have the tactical speed for it. I thought he'd be running on and collecting some nice prize-money but it was a pleasant surprise how much speed he showed to win - the sprint times from the race were very good and his finishing percentage was outstanding. He has a terrific attitude and showed that in spades at Musselburgh. I'd like to get him qualified for the novices' championship final at Sandown on the last day of the season, so I suppose I might go for a qualifier at Newbury in a few weeks' time and then look at something like the juvenile handicap at Ascot at the end of March before going on to Sandown. That would be my plan A, but if he improves in spades again and takes himself to a rating where we think we should be having a crack at something like Aintree, that would be fantastic. I think we'll play it as sensibly as we can for the time being. 12-02-25

racecards.race_name: Albert Bartlett Triple Crown Series Handicap Hurdle (Qualifier)

prev_owners.owner: McNeill Family and Prodec Networks Ltd

runners.comment: Non-runner
runners.spotlight: Won three times over hurdles in 2021 but was pulled up on all three starts in 2022 (one over fences); ran very well back from nearly two years off when second of seven finishers at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good to soft) in October, but a step backwards at Lingfield (2m4f, soft) in December; not quite sure what to expect; stable also runs Dominic's Fault; non-runner.

quotes.race: Unibet - 2021 Horserace Betting Operator Of The Year Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was tough for Tamar Bridge first time against seasoned handicappers, but he's an out-and-out stayer. He's a good horse and will make a lovely chaser in time - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Play New Slots Weekly At Betfair Casino "Newcomers" Standard Open National Hunt Flat Race (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Tamar Bridge is a big, fine horse whose future lies over further. He loved that ground and showed a good attitude - Aidan Coleman, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He left his season behind after a hard race when he won at Aintree last December. The plan is to go chasing now and he's freshened up, jumps a fence well and is hopefully going to make up into a really nice staying handicap chaser. He's ready to start and will go as soon as the rain comes as he'll need the soft ground. 27-10-22

He won his first two races this season, at Wetherby and Aintree, and in retrospect I was wrong to send him to Cheltenham in search of his hat-trick. He is on a mark only 6lb higher than his last success so I hope he can win again this season. He has the makings of a lovely chaser next season as he looks the part. 26-01-22

runners.comment: Non-runner
runners.spotlight: Successful at Leicester (2m, heavy) early last year and at Lingfield (2m, soft) in December and was still going well when brought down three out at Sandown (2m4f, soft) in January; shouldn't have a problem with the return to further; drying ground may pose a question, but he's promising; non-runner.

runners.comment: Exeter winner in December; open to improvement upped in trip and one for the shortlist
runners.spotlight: Off the mark in a maiden hurdles Exeter (2m1f, good to soft; 4-7) in December, but blundered his rider away mid-race on handicap debut at Newbury eight days ago; still open to improvement upped in trip and one for the shortlist.

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late Trevor Hemmings

runners.spotlight: Dual bumper winner who was highly tried after winning over hurdles at Stratford (2m, soft) in November 2023; probably ran better than it looked when sixth of 12 in an open handicap at Ascot (2m3f, good) in January; has undergone wind surgery since last seen and worth a second look down in grade.

runners.comment: Successful return to hurdles in January but pulled up next time; needs to bounce back
runners.spotlight: Made a successful return to hurdles at Fakenham (2m4f, good to soft) in January, but pulled up at Sandown (2m4f, soft) later in month; needs to bounce back for last year's winning stable.

quotes.race: Gamble Plant Norfolk Ltd Grand Prix Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: After Pearly Island ran over fences at Doncaster last time I suggested a try back over hurdles. It's nice to get it right sometimes - Tom Cannon, jockey.

quotes.race: Boost Your Festival Winnings @rhino.bet Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: It was a drop in class for Pearly Island and we came here quite confident as the race he finished second in at Fakenham has worked out well. The ground was soft enough for him and we'll keep going after that - Lucy Wadham, trainer.

runners.comment: A player if jumping better than last time; stable has a good recent record in this
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in his next two starts (including on handicap debut) after bolting up at Southwell (2m, heavy) in April last year, but some less-than-fluent jumping cost him at Wetherby (2m4f, soft) last month; a player if cutting out the errors this time for stable that has won three of the last five runnings.

stable_tour.quote: He was unlucky not to win a bumper last season, but he was a wide-margin winner over hurdles at Southwell in the spring. We'll stick over hurdles for now and he has the potential to progress in handicaps off a mark of 112. 06-11-24

runners.comment: 5lb above last winning mark but considered, especially if the ground continues to dry out
runners.spotlight: Won at Doncaster (2m3f, good to soft) and Aintree (2m4f, good) in the first-half of last year; best effort since returning in November when third of 14 at Hungtingdon (2m5f, soft) in January; still 5lb above her last winning mark but considered, especially if the ground continues to dry out.

quotes.race: Watch Off The Fence On attheraces.com Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qual')
quotes.quote: Alex put himself in a good position and they just fell away around him, it was a steering job which is fantastic - Mel Rowley, trainer of Masked Dance

stable_tour.quote: She lost nothing in defeat in a competitive 2m4f mares' handicap hurdle at Cheltenham last time, given that she doesn't like to be crowded in a race. She learned so much there as she was in the hustle and bustle at the moment where she didn't need it to happen. After she jumped the last hurdle, she really rallied. We weren't sure if she'd cope with the undulations, but she really powered up the hill and finished the race really well. It gives us the scope to look at those tracks as well, rather than confining ourselves to flatter courses. There's lots to look forward to and she's really matured as well. She's much easier to train now. 16-01-25

runners.comment: This trip on drying ground may be an insufficient test and vulnerable to younger rivals
runners.spotlight: Not disgraced in two of her last three starts as when fourth of eight at Chepstow (3m, soft) four weeks ago, but this trip on drying ground may be an insufficient test for her now and she looks vulnerable to younger rivals.

runners.breeder: S C E A Haras De Treli
runners.comment: Drying ground would be a positive, but needs to prove his stamina for this sort of trip
runners.spotlight: Won his first two starts after joining this yard, at Stratford (2m, good to firm) last August and at Bangor (2m1f, good) the following month; last two efforts (since wind surgery) on soft ground can be forgiven and not handicapped out of things, but he still needs to prove his stamina for this sort of trip.

runners.comment: 2m hurdle winner around here; worth keeping an eye on upped in trip for handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Made a successful hurdles debut here (2m, good) in October but out of his depth in a Grade 2 at Cheltenham later in month; better effort when third of 14 behind a promising sort at Hereford (2m, good to soft) in December and worth keeping an eye on upped in trip for handicap debut after a short break.

runners.comment: Bolted up at Wincanton last time; things may not work out so favourably this time
runners.spotlight: Made it 14th-time lucky under rules with a powerful front-running display at Wincanton (2m4f, heavy) in January, winning by 12l; rider's 10lb claim useful in view of his 11lb higher mark, but whether things will work out so favourably this time remains to be seen.

runners.comment: Second of four last time; bred to appreciate the longer trip on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Didn't show much in his early starts but better when second of four at Sandown (2m, heavy) last month (winner has since followed up in a non-event); bred to appreciate the longer trip on handicap debut and makes the shortlist.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Acca Bonus Handicap
quotes.quote: This trip will be the bare minimum for Book Of Tales but the blinkers certainly focussed his mind and he's going the right way now - Charlie Johnston, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: The Large G & T Partnership ( R Anderson Green)

runners.comment: 0-5 over hurdles; fair third at Wincanton last month but needs a bit more; cheekpieces on
runners.spotlight: 1-2 in points and 1-1 in bumpers, but 0-5 over hurdles; fair third of nine at Wincanton (3m1f, soft) last month (winner has gone in again since), but needs a bit more with cheekpieces given a go.

prev_owners.owner: J Carthy & Paul Byrne & Patrick John O'Brien

runners.comment: Made winning return from wind surgery at Southwell last month; 8lb rise asks more of him
runners.spotlight: Infrequent winner under both codes, but made the perfect return from wind surgery when successful at Southwell (2m4f, good to soft) last month; 8lb rise asks more of him, even though he has been rated 16lb higher in the past.

racecards.race_name: JCB Tele-Handler Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Stayers Hurdle Series Qualifier)

runners.comment: Rallied well at Chepstow last time, taking hurdles record to 5-12; steadily progressive
runners.spotlight: Acts on any ground; rallied well at Chepstow (2m7f) on Welsh National day when last seen, taking form figures this season to 121 and hurdles record to 5-12; steadily progressive and is 1-1 over C&D; strong claims.

quotes.race: @andythelodge Now Visited Every UK Track Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Woodie Flash can race lazily but he's travelled and jumped well today. He's obviously improved for the break and might be one we can run in a Pertemps qualifier. Olly Murphy, trainer, talking to Sky Sports.

runners.breeder: S A R L Haras Du Logis Saint Germain
runners.comment: Far from solid on recent form but could prove resurgent off current mark
runners.spotlight: Missed last season; far from solid on his form this term but has dropped in the weights and could prove resurgent off current mark, which is 4lb lower than his last winning one (three years ago).

quotes.race: Challenger Stayers Hurdle Series Final Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: An Tailliur is a great little horse who keeps on improving and likes good ground, which is key to him. He had a good few races so we had to give him a bit of a break and you could see he needed it but he hung on. He'll go through the summer, the owner is from Galway and we'll see what's there in the summer - Jonjo O'Neill, trainer.

quotes.race: Short Run Press Celebrating 40 Years Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: That was a great performance, we're happy with that so onwards and upwards. It was disappointing the last day at Cheltenham - An Tailliur was positioned out but knuckled on landing - but he's bounced back so happy days. He's a good ground horse so I'd imagine we'll put him away and go out again in the spring, maybe think about something at Cheltenham in March. You never know - Joe Hickey, racing manager to Pat Hickey, owner of An Tailliur.

quotes.race: N&L Franklin Developments Ltd Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: An Tailliur jumped really well and he's still learning as he progresses. He was obviously well in so we had to go. Dad and the team have done well finding these races for him - Jonjo O'Neill Jr - jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's won his fair share of races but he's going to find it harder now having gone up in the weights. He needs good ground and we were delighted to qualify him for the Pertemps Final when third at Cheltenham on Saturday before the ground goes against him. If the ground is suitable we'll look at what was the Fixed Brush Hurdle [now the Betfair Exchange Stayers' Handicap Hurdle] at Haydock next month and then freshen him up for the spring. We'll probably go chasing with him in either the spring or summer. 25-10-22

runners.comment: Inconsistent in the last 14 months; went close off this mark on one occasion
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent, mostly at a higher level, during the last 14 months; however, went close off this mark at Haydock (3m, good) on one occasion and has a fighting chance provided he's back to that form.

quotes.race: Unibet "You're On" Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: My Bobby Dazzler has won three here now. We were keen to give him a go over three miles. I wasn't worried about the ground for him - Philip Rowley, trainer's husband.

stable_tour.quote: He's where it all started for us. When I took out my licence he was point-to-pointing, but his owner was desperate for him to go out and do something during lockdown when there was no pointing. He was the first horse to move over into my yard and has been fantastic. He doesn't know how to run a bad race and wears his heart on his sleeve, and he deserves to carry on what he's doing. It's becoming difficult to place him where he's most competitive, but we'll keep trying to do it to the best of our ability to show what he can do in his grade. 16-01-25

runners.comment: Successful the last twice, taking overall record to 4-6; open to further improvement
runners.spotlight: Scored at Hereford (2m5f, soft) and Sandown (2m4f, heavy; gamely on handicap debut) the last twice, taking overall record to 4-6; open to further improvement; respected, assuming he stays the new trip and copes with the forecast faster ground.

quotes.race: Dragonbet The Bookmaker Of Wales National Hunt Flat Race (Cat 2 Elim') (GBB) (Conditional/Amateurs)
quotes.quote: Sole Solution has replicated the form of his full brother Easy As That who won two bumpers, including here. He's a big horse and he should be a nice horse for Sir John Timpson - Venetia Williams, trainer.

runners.comment: Ran poorly the last twice but could revive in new headgear
runners.spotlight: Chase form includes a good effort off 4lb higher in the Southern National at Fontwell (3m3f, good) on seasonal debut; two poor efforts since but could revive in new headgear; four-time hurdles winner.

runners.owner: Moorland Racing, Bill Ransom & Steve Day
runners.comment: Badly out of form; had wind surgery since last run
runners.spotlight: Listed hurdle winner in Ireland early in career; has lost his form badly and needs to derive considerable benefit from a physical tweak (wind surgery since last run); fourth outing for new yard.

runners.comment: May well improve for the first-time headgear, new trip and return to Warwick (2-3 here)
runners.spotlight: Ran dismally the last twice (chase/hurdle) but gave the impression he may well improve for headgear (now goes in cheekpieces) and this new trip; furthermore, he should benefit from the return to Warwick, being 2-3 here (0-5 elsewhere); resurgent display looks on the cards.

quotes.race: Trustatrader Apply Today Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)
quotes.quote: Nico (de Boinville) has just said Kintail is a work in progress and we are getting there with him. He is a lovely big baby. Like all those Blue Bresil's he has a laid back attitude to life. He would have learned a lot from. He is still looking around at everything that was going on, bar what was important. He will want to go do that again. All the two mile three-furlong race does is jump one hurdle in the back straight and then you are on the two-mile start. That was barely a two-mile race to me? They were going slowly over the first and to me it was like a two-mile race, but they didn't go a two-mile pace. I think the ground is quite hard work.?I wouldn't take away anything from Kintail. He just needs to learn a bit. The form of his bumper has worked out well and I think quite a lot of him as well - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won twice early last season, but we had to be patient with him later in the campaign. He wasn't 100 per cent in March, like many of our horses, and we had him all ready for weeks after that but the ground was too quick. We didn't take the chance and I'm sure that will pay off as he's going well now and has a big future. 22-10-24

racecards.race_name: Hazelton Mountford Insurance Brokers Volcano Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: G Vincent, A Geffroy & G Richardot
runners.comment: Unexposed 7yo; this longer trip should suit and he probably still has plenty more to offer
runners.spotlight: Unexposed 7yo who has already shown himself a dour stayer, as when winning on his return from six months off at Carlisle (3m2f, good to soft) in October; drying ground could pose a question, but the longer trip should suit and he probably still has plenty more to offer.

stable_tour.quote: I've always thought he'd be a better chaser than a hurdler and he proved that when winning first time over fences at Carlisle last month, staying three and a quarter miles very well. He's not a horse you want to back up too quickly because he puts a lot into his runs, but I imagine you'll see him out in December. He could end up as a regional National type. 12-11-24

runners.owner: Three Oaks, A Rose And An Acorn

prev_owners.owner: Eric Jones, Geoff Nicholas, John Romans

runners.comment: Despite some fine efforts he has gone 22 starts without a win since November 2020
runners.spotlight: Regular in marathon chases who bounced back to form when second of 14 in this headgear combination at Bangor (3m6f, soft; 40-1) last month; back up 5lb and despite some fine efforts he has gone 22 starts without a win since November 2020; others more solid.

quotes.race: mallardjewellers.com Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm thrilled to bits with The Big Breakaway, he travelled and jumped really well. He maybe found it a bit too easy over that trip - he had a little think going away from the stands with a circuit to go. Robbie has said he wouldn't mind dropping him back to two-and-a-half just to sharpen him up and make him think on his feet a little bit. That's food for thought. It was just a lovely performance to come here first time out and jump like that. I can see what Robbie is saying [drop in trip for one run], just to sharpen him up so that when he does get to the festival it doesn't all happen two gears faster. He's finding it too easy so we'll have a think and make a plan from there. Kempton seems the obvious target in my mind but we'll have a look in the calendar and make a plan. We'd probably want a couple of runs before Cheltenham to make sure it's not happening all too easily. His jumping was foot perfect and it has been since day one. If anything he jumped too well. I can't fault him, he popped when he needed to and had a bit of scope when he was asked. For a first run over fences we couldn't ask for anymore and he's got a huge future ahead of him - trainer's assistant and son Joe Tizzard

quotes.race: Conundrum EBF Stallions "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier)
quotes.quote: The Big Breakaway is a gorgeous young horse. Robbie's just said we want to be careful running him in heavy ground. We're only in the middle of December, so we could go once a month before Cheltenham. With two penalties, we'll have to step up to something hotter. We could take him to Cheltenham on January 25 to let him have a look at the course; he was bought to be a Cheltenham horse - Colin Tizzard, trainer.

quotes.race: Spectra Group Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: The Big Breakaway has excited us all the way through and has gone about that like a really nice horse, but we've got to remind ourselves he's only four. He's 17hh, so he's going to keep improving and we'll look for a race around Christmas. He's a lovely actioned horse and I'm sure he'll be better on better ground, but he can cope with that easy ground with his size and raw ability. He's not short of pace and works well at home. He's one of our nicest young horses and looks like he has a massive future - he's exciting, really exciting - Joe Tizzard, assistant trainer

stable_tour.quote: He was unlucky in the Grand National as he got knocked over at the second and his first two runs last season were right up there with his best - he had a hell of a run when second in the Welsh National. We're going to start off in the Badger Beers on Saturday, then have a shot at the Becher. I think he might just love it around Wincanton and we're going there hopeful he'll be a bit better than the horses who usually win the race. We're keen to have a spin around the Aintree fences before another shot at the National - he came down too early to know how he took to them in April. If he doesn't enjoy them we'll go back to the Welsh National. 10-11-23

He's definitely thinking about things a bit. He didn't want to know at Chepstow in the Welsh Grand National last time and it's as simple as that. I've gone back hurdling with him as we need to try and get his confidence back. We'll get him loving the game again, but he had a hard race in the Welsh National last season and it's left a mark. He then had a horrible fall in the Grand National and, when he was getting up, got knocked over again. He's a bit quirky anyway and all that didn't help. His run at Warwick on Saturday was slightly positive - he got round and stayed on. He'll have a few quick hurdle runs to get him enjoying it again. 18-01-24

runners.comment: May have been fortunate to win twice over fences since December, but remains unexposed
runners.spotlight: Has responded well to headgear and is 2-4 over fences (both wins over 3m on soft ground) since returning from a year off in November, but he was fortunate to win those races as in each case his main danger made a complete mess of the final fence; shapes like a real stayer an remains unexposed as a chaser, so not discounted.

runners.comment: Contrasting performances in his last five starts; not quite sure what to expect
runners.spotlight: Won over fences here (2m4f, good) and at Cheltenham (3m1f, soft) in 2023, but contrasting performances in his last five starts; 2lb below his last winning mark, but not quite sure what to expect.

quotes.race: John Wyke Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Are U Wise To That jumped really badly left-handed at Ascot and he threw his race away. He had been schooling lovely and straight at home. It is nice to know that he can get around Cheltenham and it definitely helped him going back left-handed. I'd say going up in trip today has helped him get into more of a routine and you would have to look at an Ultima with him. We have always liked him, but we were very disappointed after Ascot but that is the way it goes - Jonjo O'Neill, trainer.

quotes.race: racingtv.com Open Maiden National Hunt Flat Race (Category 3 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Are U Wise To That is a grand horse and done nothing wrong since he came to us. He's a big baby and quite nervy so we were delighted with that - he went through the race nicely and did everything right - Jonjo O'Neill, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's from the family of Denman and didn't have a hard season over hurdles last term as we've always thought he'd be a nice staying chaser. He made a pleasing winning debut over fences at Warwick in September but he jumped badly to his left at Ascot earlier this month, which surprised us. Nothing major has come to light and we'll keep an eye on him but we'll probably look to go left-handed next time and get him back on the right track. 14-11-23

runners.comment: Inconsistent since winning at Haydock a year ago and still 5lb higher; down the list
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent since his latest win at Haydock (3m2f, soft) a year ago and still 5lb higher; pulled up at Bangor (3m6f; soft) last month (The Big Breakaway second) and is down the list.

quotes.race: Tim Molony Memorial Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Duke Of Deception has been a different horse this year. He was really inconsistent last season for whatever reason but he seems to travel and jump a lot better. He handles the soft ground and he's going the right way - Oliver Greenall, joint trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He just got beat in the Highland National at Perth in April and we'll aim him at the local Nationals, starting in the Berkshire National at Ascot on Saturday. He likes good ground and seems to get better every season. 21-11-24

He's had two runs in point-to-points, the latter when a length-and-a-half third at Tralee in May with the first and second home being bought by Paul Nicholls and Nicky Henderson for six figures. Our fellow was a length clear at the last but was very green and was just run out of it. He's a classy, big horse and the plan is to start off in a bumper and then go straight over hurdles. 05-10-21

runners.comment: Off the same mark as when winning last time; respected if ground continues to dry out
runners.spotlight: Last four wins have come on good ground as when rallying gamely to just land a conditional jockeys' veterans' chase at Doncaster (3m) a week ago; 1-1 around here and respected off the same mark as last time, especially if conditions continue to dry out.

quotes.race: Download The At The Races App Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm quite surprised actually, as this was really a prep run before Northern Poet went chasing, to blow the cobwebs away. What the form is I'm not sure but his attitude was lovely. I would have been just as happy had he finished second or third, as we were always looking ahead. He's schooled very well over fences but after such a long layoff it was nice to give him a pipe-opener. Nick Gifford, trainer

quotes.race: Arthur Joyce Acii Intermediate Open National Hunt Flat Race
quotes.quote: The pace was generous for a change in one of these all-weather bumpers, but Northern Poet was running a bit green, so when the pace slackened off a bit I went and improved my position. When they quickened he briefly got outpaced, but he finished off well - Leighton Aspell, jockey

runners.breeder: S C E A Raymond Jean-Christian
runners.comment: 10lb below last winning mark, but plenty to prove after pulling up in his last two starts
runners.spotlight: 12yo who has been a useful chaser in his time (9-57) and is 10lb below his last winning mark, but has plenty to prove after pulling up in his last two starts.

quotes.race: LK Bennett Swinley Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Cap Du Nord is  unbelievable, he's only rated 127 but he means as much to me as a 160-rated horse. He toes-in quite badly so he was never a sales horse, he was sold to us without going to the sales but he wins a big race for us every year. Every time he gets above 130 he can't win for us, it's clear for everyone to see once it drops below that he usually ends up winning - Christian Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Handicap Chase (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Cap Du Nord ran a great race. I'm delighted. He travelled well and stayed well. I was pleased with him. - Christian Williams, trainer

quotes.race: Sir Peter O'Sullevan Memorial Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: They went very fast early on and Cap Du Nord stayed on well. He got into a nice rhythm and I thought I was a bit far back, but the pace that was on allowed us to pass a few. I think he likes to be ridden like that and he's got his own way of jumping, which can look messy, but he's safe and good. As long as the handicapper looks after him, he might nick another - Jack Tudor, jockey.

quotes.race: Young Chasers Series Final Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Cap Du Nord is a lovely horse, hopefully he's starting to come good. There's a race for him at Fakenham in Cheltenham week and he could be a Topham horse - Christian Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: Brian Ellison Racing Club Chase (A Novices' Limited Handicap) (Sedgefield Young Chaser Series Qual')
quotes.quote: Cap Du Nord had been a bit disappointing, we thought he was going to be a really nice horse. I hope he's a bit better than that, the fences came at him a bit quick round here. He jumps well at home but he got in a bit close in places here. He is declared for Catterick tomorrow and I'll have a chat with the owners, it's only 20 minutes down the road so I may stay here tonight and if he's eaten up in the morning he could run. He carries plenty of condition and if he eats his night feed and his breakfast I might run him - Christian Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Ripon Hornblower Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)

Clifford [Lee] said he felt he's got a bit more and only ever does enough. He always looked like he was outbattling the other horse. I'd imagine we'll come back for the Listed race here at the end of the month (Ripon Champion Two Years Old Trophy) - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)

Tally-Ho (stud) said the hock was no issue but cosmetically I suppose it put a lot of people off. Those Mehmas are great horses, they're tough. In his last couple of pieces of work he's just started to show us something. I thought the track or fitness might find him out today but he did it well - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: Book Tickets Online At corkracecourse.ie Handicap

We'll look for something similar, or a conditions race in the weeks ahead - Ken Condon, trainer.

We won't be too hard on him this year as I think we will benefit for it next year - Richard Hughes, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He is a lovely horse who has been placed in four of his five races. Last week at Lingfield I thought he had a winning opportunity but he was very free and had to settle for second. I think when things go his way he is the sort who can really progress and easily outperform his current mark of 74. 29-06-23

stable_tour.quote: When the yearlings come in you can usually spot the nice ones straightaway and this fellow stood out in the pack. I like his sire and he has left his stamp on this colt who is physically gorgeous, sound, strong, a good mover and has an excellent temperament. This fellow made a very pleasing debut at Haydock in May and it did him the power of good. He came forward for that and I expected a big run last week at Doncaster, when he did not disappoint with a 4L win. Potentially he could be anything as our juveniles usually come on a lot for their initial efforts. The plan immediately after that was the Superlative Stakes this week but I spoke to his owner afterwards and he is a very patient man with his horses and suggested we may wait a little longer, in which case the Listed Pat Eddery Stakes at Ascot on 24 July would be the target. This son of Churchill has always looked a cut above my others and the lads that have ridden him at home have all said he feels like a proper horse. I think he has a very bright future and could be anything. I know it is early days but he could be very smart indeed. 07-07-21

He seemed to handle the ground, I think he handled the ground at Newbury last time but I'm not sure he quite stayed so we've come back to a mile today, it looks about right. He's still a big baby and he's still learning. When he went to go, he lugged off to the right a bit. When the other horse came to him that really helped him, pushed him on and straightened him up - Maureen Haggas, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Bertinelli ran a lovely race in second and he's one to look forward to for next year as well - Chris Armstrong, representing Aidan O'Brien.

stable_tour.quote: We were delighted with him in the London Gold Cup at Newbury. He stayed on well there and we have pencilled him in for the King George V. 15-06-23

quotes.race: Byerley Stud Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (IRE Incentive Race)

He ran very green but was more professional there, the winning margin wasn't much but it's all about winning and I'm glad we have - Kevin Buckley, owners' representative.

stable_tour.quote: He won at Salisbury last season and ran well when second in the Eyrefield on his last start. He seems in good form and will probably step into a Derby trial next. 03-04-24

stable_tour.quote: His form is holding up very well. We didn't go hurdling with him last season, even though he was the age he was, as we felt we would be better off waiting for this season. He has progressed nicely through his bumpers and his form is working out great. He's got a nice turn of foot and hopefully he can continue over hurdles in the smart sort of form he left bumpers in. We've high hopes for him. 25-11-24

He'd been going well at home before his debut at Leopardstown over Christmas, so we were not surprised he ran so well. Patrick and I were very impressed with how he won there. We then missed the next meeting, so he goes for the Champion Bumper without another race, but he is very much all about the future. You have to be impressed by the speed he showed at Leopardstown and although his stablemate will be the horse most people will focus on, this horse is smart. 09-03-22

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Today Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

quotes.race: Copper Horse Handicap
quotes.quote: I was so disappointed with My Lyka [19th in the Ascot Stakes] and I was wondering, could Belloccio make up for it? Then I was disappointed when he didn't jump out as fast as I hoped, but William didn't panic. He waited until the race was starting in earnest and produced him with a perfect run. This fellow will probably go to the Ebor. He's entered here on Saturday, but we won't make any decisions about this weekend yet. We'll see how he comes out of this race, and I think the bigger picture may come into it. The long-term aim might be to qualify for the Melbourne Cup. We'll see how things go and I'll have another word with William - Willie Mullins, trainer.

quotes.race: Tuesday Treat At Punchestown Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Belloccio brought a good level of form to the race, showed a good attitude for jumping and did it nicely. He will have no problem adjusting, he will be learning on the job a little bit. If they get him going he should be smart - Paul Townend, rider,

stable_tour.quote: He is very similar to Wonderful Tonight in that he wants 1m4f and soft ground. The day he gets his conditions he will put up a very different level of form to last time. As a two-year-old he won both starts, the latter a Listed race at Toulouse, but this year things have not been in his favour. His first run back was in the Sandown Classic Trial, where he lost a shoe and came back very sore for a while. I felt he ran a stormer next time out in the Dante despite the going as we had nowhere else to go. Now he is ready to go again but I am going to wait for the rain and do the right thing by the horse. I have a lot of time for him and he is possibly the best three-year-old I have ever trained, which I know sounds a big statement when you consider Wonderful Tonight, won two Group 1s last year, but I really believe he has that potential. When he gets everything in his favour he will raise a few eyebrows and we have him in at Royal Ascot as well as the Grand Prix de Paris [on July 14] and then we have to decide whether to go down the St Leger route as there are a lot of stayers in his family or shorter, when the Arc could be an option. The form of his Listed win last year has taken quite a boost as the runner-up, Cirona, subsequently won a Group 3 and was a head second in the Group 1 Prix Saint-Alary at Longchamp. Olivier Peslier rode him on that occasion and he regularly rings me up to inquire how the horse is doing, which pretty much says it all. Keep an eye out for him as I am sure he'll be worth the wait. 02-06-21
